scenario.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
scenario.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is finite and the assessment counts rounds expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy. Classifications can change in either direction during the run, and a track released to you late still has to be fought in its proper place in the queue.

The raid is already on top of you as you take the seat. The first valid solution is available within seconds of the clock starting and the waves overlap from then on. You have 315 seconds. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep and already classified. Crosses the 70 km long-range ring at about T+21, the 20 km short ring at about T+194 and the 5 km inner limit at about T+246 if unengaged.
Second fast closer, up at zero and marginally ahead of the lead in ring terms: reaches the 70 km ring at about T+14, which is the first valid firing solution of the run. Inner limit at about T+248.

Fastest and highest of the three, but enters unclassified: fire must be held on it until the referral answer comes back Enemy at about T+42, by which time it is already inside the 70 km ring at roughly 68 km. Crosses the long-range ring at about T+36, the short ring at about T+198, inner limit about T+247. It rejoins a queue the other two jets are already occupying.

First of the unmanned wave, appearing before the lead jet has a solution. Already inside the medium ring and reads as the nearest track on the display; short ring at about T+59, inner limit about T+186.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Short ring about T+81, inner limit about T+202.
Low-mid altitude; marginal against a badly set tilt. Short ring about T+61, inner limit about T+194.
Arrives while the jet queue is still saturated. Short ring about T+117, inner limit about T+241 — the longest-running of the unmanned wave.
Southern flank, low, crosses the 20 km short ring at about T+63 — within twenty seconds of appearing. Inner limit about T+201.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector. Short ring about T+111, inner limit about T+230.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge and low, and it appears already on the 20 km short ring — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit about T+212.

Never resolves unaided. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard with heading and altitude changes that read as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+97 and overflies near T+159. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification.

Low and slow on the southern flank, crossing rather than closing; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+70.

Appears inside the medium ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, in the thick of the queue. Resolves only at about T+125, after more than a minute and a half of ambiguity; reaches the inner limit around T+204.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers destroyed inside the 315-second window, each engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system permits — for the track released late, that means the first solution after it is classified Enemy, not before; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the 5 km inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown or a friendly is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven interceptors may be expended.

result.notes: Arrivals are pulled hard forward: the first valid firing solution now falls at T+14 instead of T+51 (jets respawned at 74–80 km rather than ~79–85 km), and the unmanned wave now enters between T+8 and T+66 instead of T+15 and T+92, so the picture is saturated inside the first minute. The window stays at 315 s because that is the enforced floor for the 600-kt track against the 70 km envelope ((70×1.25)÷0.30864÷0.9 = 315) — slowing the fastest track would raise the floor, not lower it, so the only honest compression was earlier arrivals; the brief's stale '195 seconds' figure and the matching resource line are corrected to 315. For the second complaint, hostile jet TN-4103 now enters as Unknown and is only released as Enemy at T+42, when it has already crossed inside the 70 km ring at about 68 km — fire must be held on it until it is inside the envelope, and it then has to be slotted back into a queue the other two jets already occupy.
requests: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
One of the hostiles should hold fire discipline until it is inside the engagement envelope.
